candidates.explanation: The refresh flow takes sessionId and hash from the refresh JWT and issues a new token pair (getTokensData at ~546). Replaying the old refresh token still works, so the old hash is not being enforced or rotated. Either the check that the session's stored hash equals the token's hash is missing or wrong, or the session isn't updated with the new hash after the new pair is issued. The old token's hash therefore stays valid. I could not see the function body, so this is inferred from the signature and the call to getTokensData.

This signs the refresh token with the session id and hash. If refreshToken passes it the old hash, or the hash isn't regenerated per rotation, the new refresh token is equivalent to the old one and both stay valid.
The strategy only validates the JWT signature and expiry and returns the payload. It doesn't check the session state. All rotation enforcement therefore depends on AuthService.refreshToken.

fix.description: In AuthService.refreshToken, load the session by sessionId and throw UnauthorizedException if it is missing or if session.hash !== data.hash. Then generate a new random hash (for example sha256 of a random string). Issue the new tokens with that hash. Persist it with sessionService.update(session.id, { hash }) so the previous refresh token is invalidated. I could not see the function body, so confirm which of these steps is missing.
